mixed_classes_warm_instruction_increase.finding: Final AArch64 machine code separates the transition-vector length and stride loads: the baseline uses one paired load, while the candidate uses two scalar loads. Debug line profiles record exactly 65,537 additional instructions in the inlined vector-to-slice conversion, matching one extra instruction per cached transition. This identifies a per-byte scan cost from changed cache layout, rather than an assertion-evaluation or compile/preparation cost.

baseline_machine_code.meaning: load transition vector length (offset 0x88) and stride (offset 0x90)

interpretation_limits: This explains the generated-code instruction increase for this workload and this AArch64 compiler/build. It does not imply a universal wall-clock slowdown.

Native Criterion comparisons sampled direct mode, not the forced-class mixed case. Direct mixed timings did not significantly regress; forced-class native throughput was not measured in this final timing pass.
The remaining 461 instructions were not isolated to individual stream-preparation, EOF or cleanup operations.
mixed_classes_warm_instruction_increase.status: Historical diagnosis before final layout fix; no longer the final performance result.

historical_near_limit_timing_variability.scope: Before cache-layout-only change; preserved to show process-to-process variability, not a final-source measurement.

layout_fix.change: repr(C) Tier1DfaCache with inner, transitions, stride, dead_transitions, targets in that order. Correctness does not depend on Vec internal order.
layout_fix.remaining_delta_qualification: The extra per-transition instruction is gone; the remaining 485 instructions per measured 64 KiB stream were not isolated individually.

final_performance_interpretation.native_comparison_policy: Retained both initial final-source comparisons and exactly one fresh paired repeat of the three flagged native cases and all three near-limit shapes. No additional repeat was selected to obtain a desired result.
final_performance_interpretation.native_estimate_format: time_seconds_95ci_point contains the printed interval endpoints and point estimate; Criterion prints regression slope for these cases, whereas its change percentage compares means. Those two point ratios can differ, especially with outliers.
final_performance_interpretation.direct_scan_outliers: Initial nonword warm +3.03% and mixed warm +3.52% were not reproduced: fresh paired changes were -0.83% (within noise threshold) and -0.94% (no change detected). Treat these small native differences as uncertain; do not claim universal zero overhead.
final_performance_interpretation.small_compile_end: Initial +2.54%; fresh +3.32% with interval +0.96..+7.10% and Criterion classification within noise threshold. Retain this small measured build-time difference; instruction count improves.

near_limit_simple_tails.conclusion: Both final-source rounds show a build-time increase; retain the fresh +6.30% / about 49.58 us as an explicit bounded compile tradeoff, with substantial baseline/process variability. No further native repeat was performed.

final_performance_interpretation.forced_classes_mixed: Fresh baseline/candidate native comparison improves -2.93% (95% CI -4.77..-1.48%). Final Callgrind increase is +0.02052%, after verified removal of the extra per-transition load instruction.
final_performance_interpretation.remaining_reengage_increase: The historically named tier3_rule_text workload automatically selects GroupedStream in both builds. Its +3.31894% instruction increase is unchanged by the cache-layout fix, below the unchanged gate, and attributable almost entirely to prefilter/NEON generated code: the candidate calls memclass_neon out of line where the baseline profile attributes the NEON work to the inlined prefilter. This remains a measured cross-engine generated-code cost; no SIMD change was made.

reengage_largest_increase_investigation.actual_backend: GroupedStream (automatic selection in cases::scan via memory.matcher(re))
reengage_largest_increase_investigation.finding: The profile attributes baseline NEON work to Prefilter::find (inlined) and candidate NEON work to separately called memclass_neon functions. Summing every source-file attribution for those functions accounts for 99.95% of the whole-benchmark instruction increase. This supports a generated-code/inlining cost, not an increase in assertion evaluation work. No native timing comparison for this existing reengage workload was added.
reengage_largest_increase_investigation.policy: Retained under the unchanged gate; no unrelated SIMD implementation or inlining attribute change.
